scams.name: The Via dell'Indipendenza "Cigarette" Pickpocket
scams.description: Pairs of women on Via dell'Indipendenza interrupt tourists asking for a cigarette, the time, or directions while a partner pickpockets the wallet or bag. A June 2016 Il Resto del Carlino arrest documented two Roma women (ages 18 and 26) using this exact MO on a Japanese tourist; a September 2025 r/bologna firsthand post and an August 2025 CCTV arrest on Via Riva di Reno confirm the female-duo pattern is still active in 2025.
scams.avoidance: On Via dell'Indipendenza, walk on the portico-wall side with your bag between you and the wall. Reply to any 'posso fare una domanda' with a firm 'no, mi scusi' and keep walking. Use a crossbody bag with the zipper facing your body. Shout 'ladri!' if a theft is in progress — Bologna police actively patrol this street. Never carry a wallet in a back pocket in the historic center.
scams.location: Via dell'Indipendenza (Piazza del Nettuno to Bologna Centrale), Via Ugo Bassi, connecting porticoed streets

scams.name: The Due Torri "Spare Some Change" Arm-Grab
scams.description: Beggars at Piazza di Porta Ravegnana — directly under the Torre degli Asinelli and Torre Garisenda — grab tourists' arms during a pretended plea for alms and empty pockets in the same motion. An August 2016 Il Resto del Carlino arrest (44-year-old Bosnian woman with prior convictions, 6pm, Spanish tourist) established the MO; a Bolognatoday report of a Japanese tourist restraining a thief in the same piazza confirms it repeats. A 3am variant turns violent — a 43-year-old French woman was slapped and robbed in the historic center.
scams.avoidance: Compose your upward-looking tower photo before stopping — phone out, zip closed, bag in hand. Step back one full pace if anyone making a begging gesture enters your body space. Never let a stranger touch you in the historic center. Carry a daily-use wallet with €40–€60 and keep cards, passport, and larger cash in a flat pouch under your shirt. Call 112 immediately if robbed.
scams.location: Piazza di Porta Ravegnana (Due Torri), Via Rizzoli, Piazza della Mercanzia

scams.name: Bologna Centrale Platform & Taxi-Queue Pickpockets
scams.description: Coordinated groups work Bologna Centrale platforms, underground passages, ticket machines and the taxi queue. Train staff now announce 'attenzione, pickpocket!' as trains pull in. A July 2024 incident saw a Business-class suitcase stolen from a Frecciarossa during the ~10-minute Bologna Centrale stop. Variants include 'helper' scams at FastTicket kiosks that photograph card PINs and three-to-five-person distraction teams that open outer luggage pouches on platforms.
scams.avoidance: Exit via the main Piazza delle Medaglie d'Oro entrance, not Via Carracci (Bolognina/rear). Take only official white taxis from the signed rank; ignore any 'taxi?' offers inside the hall. Use only Trenitalia or Italo apps or their logo-marked machines for tickets. Keep luggage on the facing end-of-carriage rack on Frecciarossa/Italo. Never buy tickets from third-party resellers.
scams.location: Bologna Centrale platforms, underground passages, main entrance forecourt, taxi queue; Via Amendola; Via Matteotti

scams.name: The Outdoor Restaurant Bag-Snatch
scams.description: Bags hung on chair backs at outdoor Quadrilatero and Jewish Ghetto restaurants are snatched by passing pedestrians, followed by immediate ATM cashout before cards can be frozen. A June 2017 Il Resto del Carlino arrest documented a 22-year-old Moroccan man snatching a 53-year-old American tourist's purse on Via Volturno; police caught him on Via dei Mille with her Gucci wallet, €70 cash, credit cards, and a $500 check. A Bolognatoday 'Furto nel Ghetto' report documents the ATM-cashout variant on Via de' Giudei.
scams.avoidance: Place your bag on the floor with one strap looped around your chair leg or ankle — never on the chair back or an empty seat. Sit with your back to a wall facing foot traffic. Leave your passport in the hotel safe. Use in-app card blocks immediately if a bag disappears — the ATM variant depends on a 3–10 minute reaction lag. Eat where locals eat; avoid the Piazza-Maggiore-to-Piazza-della-Mercanzia alleys flagged as '95% tourist traps' on r/bologna.
scams.location: Outdoor tables on Via Volturno, Via dei Mille, Via de' Giudei (Jewish Ghetto), Via Pescherie Vecchie, Quadrilatero market streets

scams.name: The Bologna Taxi Overcharge
scams.description: Bologna Airport drivers quote flat fares above the posted €12.80 fixed fare (up to 6km) or switch the meter to a long-distance tariff inside the city. A 2025 r/bologna thread documents a €24 starting fare — a fellow commenter calls it 'straight up scammed.' The true max radio starting fare is €6.80; per-km is €1.45 in normal daytime. Variants include the 'credit card reader is broken' scam that forces victims to withdraw cash at ATMs while the driver watches the PIN.
scams.avoidance: Use the Marconi Express monorail (€12.20, ~7 minutes) from the airport to Bologna Centrale — it is faster and has nothing to negotiate. For taxis, use only white-painted Cotabo or Taxi Bologna at the official rank and confirm the €12.80 airport fixed fare before closing the door. Use TaxiClick or Cotabo (051.372727) for radio calls. Always demand a ricevuta with taxi number, time, and route. Refuse any ATM detour.
scams.location: Bologna Guglielmo Marconi Airport taxi rank, Bologna Centrale rank, radio-dispatched taxis from suburbs

scams.name: The Quadrilatero "Ancient" Tourist-Menu Trap
scams.description: Quadrilatero restaurants add unmarked per-person coperto (often above €3.50), automatic 15% 'servizio' on foreign cards, unrequested pane/acqua/antipasti, and fish or steak priced 'al etto' that arrives at 400–600g. A 2024 NYT opinion piece documents 'Ancient cold cuts butcher' chain shops that had actually 'been open for three months.' r/bologna locals name the Piazza-Maggiore-to-Piazza-della-Mercanzia alleys as '95% tourist traps.'
scams.avoidance: Walk 3–5 minutes off the Piazza Maggiore axis — Via del Pratello, Santo Stefano, or Mercato delle Erbe are locally recommended. Photograph the posted menu outside before sitting (Italian law requires prices). Ask at seating: 'mi conferma il coperto e se c'è servizio?' Prefer trattorias/osterias with handwritten daily menus. Trust Italian-language Google reviews sorted by Most Recent over English reviews.
scams.location: Via Pescherie Vecchie, Via Drapperie, Via Clavature, Via degli Orefici, Via Caprarie (Quadrilatero)

scams.name: The Fake Short-Term-Rental / Key Handoff
scams.description: Fraudulent hosts on Airbnb, Booking and TripAdvisor direct guests off-platform for payment, then vanish on arrival day. TripAdvisor Bologna Forum's 'Be aware of scams' thread documents a victim contacted by 'Bjarne' via off-platform email; a 'SCAM. DO NOT BOOK' review names a Fiera-district apartment that was locked and unresponsive on arrival. Side patterns: undisclosed credit-card surcharges and a fake 'city tax in cash' cover (Bologna's real €5/night tourism tax applies only to rooms over €120/night).
scams.avoidance: Book only through Airbnb, Booking.com, or platforms with pay-through-platform guarantees — never wire or pay cash off-platform. Check the property on Google Street View before arrival. Require in-platform messages with photos of the entrance and keybox. Budget for the €5/night tourism tax (rooms over €120/night only); refuse cash 'city fee' surprises. Push back on credit-card surcharges — EU PSD2 bars them on most consumer cards and legitimate B&Bs don't ask.
scams.location: Apartment listings in the historic center, Fiera district, areas within 15 minutes' walk of Bologna Centrale
